property_summary: After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether, when block.timestamp equals pastBlockTime (same timestamp as previous call), the reference reverts due to require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) while the buggy version does not revert and updates pastBlockTime to the same value.
After two calls to fallback with 10 ether each at the same timestamp (block.timestamp == pastBlockTime), the reference reverts while the buggy version updates pastBlockTime.

After a block with block.number % 15 == 0 and a fallback call with 10 ether, the 'send' variant fails to transfer remaining balance and thus allows a second call in the same block to succeed, resetting pastBlockTime while the reference contract's transfer reverts, leading to different pastBlockTime values.

After a block where block.number % 15 == 0, first fallback call with 10 ether succeeds, but 'send' fails silently; a second fallback call in same block succeeds in M reverting in P, so pastBlockTime differs.

After a fallback call in a block where block.number % 15 == 0 succeeds, a second fallback call with 10 ether in the same block reverts in the reference (due to transfer reverting the whole call) but succeeds in the mutant (due to send silently failing), causing pastBlockTime to be updated only in the mutant.

After a successful fallback call in a block where block.number % 15 == 0, a second fallback call with 10 ether in the same block reverts in the reference (transfer reverts the whole transaction) but succeeds in the mutant (send fails silently), updating pastBlockTime only in the mutant, so pastBlockTime values diverge.

After two fallback calls with 10 ether in the same block where block.number % 15 != 0, only the first call succeeds (block.timestamp increases), and the second call reverts due to require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime); therefore pastBlockTime is set to the first call's timestamp.

After a call to fallback with msg.value = 0, the reference contract reverts because the require(msg.value == 10 ether) fails, while the buggy contract passes the check and executes the rest, causing pastBlockTime to be updated, which can later be observed via the public getter pastBlockTime().

After two calls to fallback with 10 ether each, the reference contract transfers balance only when block.number % 15 == 0, while the buggy contract transfers when block.number % 15 != 0; by setting block.number to 1 (first call, %15 != 0) then 16 (second call, %16 %15 == 0), the reference retains balance after the second call (transfer only on first) but the buggy version transfers after both, leaving zero balance.

After a single fallback call with 10 ether at block.number=1 (where 1%15 != 0) the reference (transfer only on %15==0) keeps the balance, while the buggy version (transfer on %15!=0) sends it all, leaving address(c).balance different.
